questions.stem: A 32-year-old male who is being treated for acute leukemia develops oliguria. His serum creatinine level is 2.7mg/dL. Renal biopsy reveals multiple uric acid crystals obstructing the renal tubular lumen. The principal site of uric acid precipitation would be which of the following?

options.label: A
options.text: Proximal tubules due to high solute concentration (25%)

options.label: B
options.text: Proximal tubules due to impaired uric acid transport (20%)

options.label: C
options.text: Loop of Henle due to hyposmolarity (7%)

options.label: D
options.text: Collecting ducts due to low urine pH (43%)

questions.answerText: Collecting ducts due to low urine pH (43%)
questions.solutionHtml:
Collecting ducts due to low urine pH (43%)
  • Uric acid is soluble at physiological pH. The lowest pH along the nephron is found in the distal tubules and collecting ducts; So these are the segments that become obstructed by uric acid crystals.


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 676

questions.stemHtml: Aldosterone is the mineralocorticoid steroid hormone produced by the zona glomerulosa of the adrenal cortex in the adrenal gland. It plays a central role in the homeostatic regulation of blood pressure, plasma sodium (Na+), and potassium (K+) levels. In the image given below, parts of the nephron are labeled in the alphabet.Select the parts that are the site of action of aldosterone?

options.label: A
options.text: E and F

options.label: B
options.text: F and G

options.label: C
options.text: E and G

options.label: D
options.text: Only E

questions.answerText: E and F
questions.solutionHtml:
E and F
  • E and F correspond to the late distal tubule and collecting tubule. Aldosterone acts on these sites.
  • The second half of the distal tubule and subsequent cortical collecting tubule have similar functional characteristics. Anatomically, they are composed of two distinct cell types, principal cells, and intercalated cells.


Guyton and Hall Textbook of physiology, 14th Edition, Page No.352-53.

questions.stem: The thick ascending limb of the Loop of Henle and the early distal convoluted tubule are parts of the nephron. The early DCT is lined with the simple cuboidal cells while in the ascending limb epithelium is simple squamous epithelium. Both parts are actively involved in urine formation. Select the common characteristics of both parts in urine formation?

options.label: A
options.text: Impermeable to water

options.label: B
options.text: Active reabsorption of sodium and chloride ions from the filtrate into the interstitium

options.label: C
options.text: Impermeable to sodium and chloride ions

options.label: D
options.text: Both A and B have common characteristics

questions.answerText: Both A and B have common characteristics
questions.solutionHtml:
Both A and B have common characteristics
  • First, assume that the loop of Henle is filled with a fluid having a concentration of 300 mOsm/L, the same as that leaving the proximal tubule. Next, the active ion pump of the thick ascending limb on the loop of Henle reduces the concentration inside the tubule and raises the interstitial concentration; this pump establishes a 200-mOsm/ L concentration gradient between the tubular fluid and interstitial fluid.


Guyton and Hall Textbook of physiology, 14th Edition, Page No. 367-368.

questions.stemHtml: A human nephron is shown in an image representing the anatomic location structure of DCT. The distal convoluted tubule (DCT) is divided into early and late segments, termed DCT1 and DCT2, respectively. The connecting tubule (CNT) is located immediately downstream of the DCT2.Select the improper features of DCT1 and DCT2?

options.label: A
options.text: DCT 1 forms the macula densa which is part of the JG apparatus

options.label: B
options.text: DCT 2 is highly convoluted with reabsorptive features as those of thick segments of the ascending limb of the loop

options.label: C
options.text: DCT 2 permeable to water

options.label: D
options.text: DCT 2 is called a diluting segment of the nephron

questions.answerText: DCT 2 permeable to water
questions.solutionHtml:
DCT 2 permeable to water
  • The next part of the distal tubule is highly convoluted and has many of the same reabsorptive characteristics of the thick segment of the ascending limb of the loop of Henle. That is, it avidly reabsorbs most of the ions, including sodium, potassium, and chloride, but is virtually impermeable to water and urea. For this reason, it is referred to as the diluting segment because it also dilutes the tubular fluid.



Guyton and Hall Textbook of physiology,14th Edition, Page No. 351.

questions.stem: The distal convoluted tubule is structurally and functionally divisible into two parts. Early DCT and late DCT have specific functions in the process of urine formation. The late DCT performs a function similar to the function of the thick ascending limb of the Loop of Henle. The late DCT possesses characteristic transporters essential for its reabsorptive functions. Select the best-suited justification for transporters in late DCT in nephron?

options.label: A
options.text: Occurrence of sodium-chloride cotransporter in the luminal surface of DCT cells

options.label: B
options.text: Transport of sodium and chloride ions from the tubular lumen into the cells of late DCT

options.label: C
options.text: Na+-K+ ATPase pump exports sodium ions across the basolateral surfaces of cells of late DCT into the interstitium

options.label: D
options.text: All best are suited

questions.answerText: All best are suited
questions.solutionHtml:
All best are suited

All justifications are best suited to the function of the late DCT portion of the nephron.



Guyton and Hall Textbook of physiology, 14th Edition, Page No. 351-353.

questions.stem: A male patient at the age of 46 years reported muscle soreness, spasms in leg muscles, numbness in fingers and toes, excessive thirst, and increased frequency of passing urine in the past 2 months. Biochemical parameters serum sodium 150 mmol/L, serum potassium 2.5mmol/L, mild proteinuria, and GFR 120 ml/min were reported. Urine analysis neutral or slightly alkaline urine, urinary potassium concentration was 35 mmol/L. Select the correct statements?

options.label: A
options.text: Excess aldosterone secretion

options.label: B
options.text: Associated with sodium retention

options.label: C
options.text: Increased tubular secretion of potassium

options.label: D
options.text: All correct

questions.answerText: All correct
questions.solutionHtml:
All correct
  • Manifestations are suggestive of Conn syndrome.
  • Excess aldosterone secretion, as occurs in patients with adrenal tumors (Conn syndrome), is associated with sodium retention and decreased plasma potassium concentration due, in part, to excessive potassium secretion by the kidneys.


Guyton and Hall Textbook of physiology, 14th Edition, Page No. 358-359.

questions.stem: Endocrinologist presented a case of a female patient in 34 years with thin skin, central obesity, hypertension, plethoric moon facies, purple striae and easy bruisability, and glucose intolerance. Hematopoietic features of hypercortisolism include leukocytosis, lymphopenia, and eosinopenia. Select the best explanation for Cushing's disease?

options.label: A
options.text: Benign adrenal adenoma secreting excess ACTH increased the production of cortisol from the adrenal cortex.

options.label: B
options.text: Benign pituitary adenoma secreting excess levels of cortisol.

options.label: C
options.text: Benign adrenal adenoma secreting excess levels of cortisol

options.label: D
options.text: Benign pituitary adenoma secreting excess ACTH, increased production of cortisol from the adrenal cortex.

questions.answerText: Benign pituitary adenoma secreting excess ACTH, increased production of cortisol from the adrenal cortex.
questions.solutionHtml:
Benign pituitary adenoma secreting excess ACTH, increased production of cortisol from the adrenal cortex.
  • The benign pituitary adenoma secreting excess ACTH, increased production of cortisol from the adrenal cortex. The manifestations listed in the statement are suggestive of Cushing syndrome.


Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 20th Edition, Page No. 2726-27

questions.stemHtml: Endocrinologists presented a case of a woman at age 57 years with hyperpigmentation on her face as in the image and characteristic sites of darkening are skin creases. Select the one that is an improper explanation of Addison’s disease?

options.label: A
options.text: Either glucocorticoid or mineralocorticoid deficiency may come first, but eventually, all patients fail to secrete aldosterone and normal cortisol secretion

options.label: B
options.text: Hyponatremia

options.label: C
options.text: Hyperkalemia

options.label: D
options.text: Severe hypotension

questions.answerText: Either glucocorticoid or mineralocorticoid deficiency may come first, but eventually, all patients fail to secrete aldosterone and normal cortisol secretion
questions.solutionHtml:
Either glucocorticoid or mineralocorticoid deficiency may come first, but eventually, all patients fail to secrete aldosterone and normal cortisol secretion

Image describes

  • A 57-year-old female presented with symptoms of primary adrenal insufficiency secondary to autoimmune Addison’s Diffuse skin hyperpigmentation had developed, as illustrated by her facial appearance.
  • The hands demonstrate increased pigmentation of the palmar creases and wrists compared to healthy female control (far right).
  • With long-term glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid therapy, her hyperpigmentation resolved, as shown by the normal palmar skin pigmentation in the patient. Of note, she wears a medical bracelet indicating her requirement for glucocorticoids in case of severe illness.


Davidson’s Principles & Practice of Medicine, 23rd Edition, Page No.693-94

questions.stem: Select the best-suited differentiating statements between primary hyperaldosteronism from secondary hyperaldosteronism?

options.label: A
options.text: With renin high and aldosterone high (secondary hyperaldosteronism)

options.label: B
options.text: With renin low and aldosterone high (primary hyperaldosteronism

options.label: C
options.text: Inadequate renal perfusion (diuretic therapy, cardiac failure, liver failure, nephrotic syndrome, renal artery stenosis in secondary hyperaldosteronism

options.label: D
options.text: All are best-suited statements

questions.answerText: All are best-suited statements
questions.solutionHtml:
All are best-suited statements

Davidson’s Principles & Practice of Medicine, 23rd Edition, Page No. 694

questions.stem: Physiologists determined the reabsorption of sodium ions by the cells of proximal convoluted tubules. He described the initial step in The passive entry of Na+ into the PCT cell across the apical membrane. Select the incorrect?

options.label: A
options.text: Intracellular Na+ concentration ([Na+]i) is low

options.label: B
options.text: Cell voltage is positive with respect to the lumen

options.label: C
options.text: Passive entry of Na+ into the cell across the apical membrane

options.label: D
options.text: Transcellular mode of sodium reabsorption

questions.answerText: Cell voltage is positive with respect to the lumen
questions.solutionHtml:
Cell voltage is positive with respect to the lumen
  • The statement "Cell voltage is positive with respect to the lumen" is incorrect. The cell voltage is negative with respect to the lumen.


Guyton and Hall, 14th Edition, Page No. 342-43,

questions.stem: Physiologists studied the effect of sodium reabsorption by cells of proximal convoluted tubules in healthy experimental rats. He concluded that kidneys excrete 95% of the ingested Na at rates that match dietary Na intake. Select the incorrect features that enable epithelial cells of PCT in sodium reabsorption?

options.label: A
options.text: Renal tubule cells are held by tight junction

options.label: B
options.text: Lateral intercellular spaces lie behind the tight junctions and separate the epithelial cells of the tubule.

options.label: C
options.text: Sodium is the solute that moves by both transcellular and paracellular pathways

options.label: D
options.text: Sodium is the solute that moves by only paracellular pathway

questions.answerText: Sodium is the solute that moves by only paracellular pathway
questions.solutionHtml:
Sodium is the solute that moves by only paracellular pathway
  • The incorrect statement is D. Sodium can move by both transcellular and paracellular pathways in the cells of the proximal convoluted tubule.
  • Sodium ions can move by both transcellular and paracellular pathways


Guyton and Hall textbook of physiology, 14th Edition, Page No.344

questions.stem: A male person of age 23 years reported manifestations of passing glucose in urine which he found incidentally in a lab test. Examination and other tests revealed the absence of other manifestations of renal disease. The condition was labeled as isolated renal glycosuria in patients. Select the incorrect reabsorption of glucose by epithelial cells of PCT?

options.label: A
options.text: Active transport can move a solute against an electrochemical gradient; this requires energy

options.label: B
options.text: Reabsorption of glucose by the renal tubule is an example of secondary active transport

options.label: C
options.text: Primary active transport mediates the reabsorption of glucose in the renal tubule

options.label: D
options.text: The renal threshold for glucose (RTg) corresponds to a blood glucose level of ~180 mg/dL

questions.answerText: Primary active transport mediates the reabsorption of glucose in the renal tubule
questions.solutionHtml:
Primary active transport mediates the reabsorption of glucose in the renal tubule

Primary active transport does not mediate the reabsorption of glucose in the renal tubule



Guyton and Hall textbook of physiology, 14th Edition, Page No. 344

questions.stem: The patient at the age of 34 years presented with nausea, vomiting, edema on the face and feet, and low urine output past several weeks. The patient gave H/O for taking medication for the infection in the throat a few days earlier. Examination reported renal failure and decided to estimate the glomerular filtration rate in patients. Select the incorrect?

options.label: A
options.text: Para-amino hippuric acid diagnostic for renal failure

options.label: B
options.text: A healthy person can clear about 90% of the PAH from the plasma flowing through the kidneys

options.label: C
options.text: Clearance of PAH from plasma is elevated in renal failure patient

options.label: D
options.text: PAH clearance can be used to estimate the renal plasma flow

questions.answerText: Clearance of PAH from plasma is elevated in renal failure patient
questions.solutionHtml:
Clearance of PAH from plasma is elevated in renal failure patient
  • The rate of clearance of PAH from plasma is reduced in renal failure patients due to reduced glomerular filtration rate.


Guyton and Hall textbook of physiology 14th edition, pp 350.

questions.stem: Endocrinologist presented a case of polyuria, polydipsia, lethargy, and dyslipidemia with hypertension in a male patient at the age of 67 years. Examination and lab tests were conducted and the patient was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. Endocrinologists explained the clinical significance of transport maximum for glucose in renal cells. Select the incorrect?

options.label: A
options.text: Transport maximum is due to saturation of the specific transporters

options.label: B
options.text: The transport maximum for the glucose tubular transport system in adult humans is about 275 mg/min.

options.label: C
options.text: Under the normal healthy conditions, no traceable amount of glucose is excreted by tubules

options.label: D
options.text: The filtered load of glucose is only about 125 mg/min

questions.answerText: The transport maximum for the glucose tubular transport system in adult humans is about 275 mg/min.
questions.solutionHtml:
The transport maximum for the glucose tubular transport system in adult humans is about 275 mg/min.
  • The transport maximum for the glucose tubular transport system in adult humans is about 375 mg/min.


Guyton and Hall textbook of physiology, 14th Edition, Page No.346.

questions.stem: Water moves across the tight junctions in epithelial cells of PCT by passive diffusion. Physiologists reported a new event that describes the movement of a few solutes with water. Select the correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Solvent drag

options.label: B
options.text: Facilitative diffusion

options.label: C
options.text: Transcellular transport

options.label: D
options.text: Co-transport

questions.answerText: Solvent drag
questions.solutionHtml:
Solvent drag
  • Solvent drag, also known as bulk transport, refers to solutes in the ultrafiltrate that are transported back from the renal tubule by the flow of water rather than specifically by ion pumps or other membrane transport proteins.
  • This is a phenomenon primarily in renal physiology, but it also occurs in gastrointestinal physiology.


Guyton and Hall textbook of physiology, 14th Edition,Page No.347-348.

questions.stemHtml: The image given below represents podocytes or pedicels. Podocytes are cells in the visceral layer of Bowman's capsule. These cells surround the capillaries of the glomerulus. Select the incorrect?

options.label: A
options.text: Formation of filtration slits in Bowman’s capsule

options.label: B
options.text: Inhibit passage of macromolecules through slits

options.label: C
options.text: Secrete basement membrane

options.label: D
options.text: Helpful in reabsorption

questions.answerText: Helpful in reabsorption
questions.solutionHtml:
Helpful in reabsorption
  • Podocytes are found lining the Bowman's capsules in the nephrons of the kidney. The foot processes known as pedicels that extend from the podocytes wrap themselves around the capillaries of the glomerulus to form the filtration slits.


Ganong’s Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No.1539

questions.stemHtml: Physiologists in a lecture described the ability of nephrons to alter the concentration of urine. Some features of the mechanism are in the image below, Select the incorrect?

options.label: A
options.text: System in which the inflow runs in a loop with outflow

options.label: B
options.text: System in which inflow is counter to outflow

options.label: C
options.text: Inflow is in close proximity to the outflow

options.label: D
options.text: Alter the concentration gradient of urine

questions.answerText: System in which the inflow runs in a loop with outflow
questions.solutionHtml:
System in which the inflow runs in a loop with outflow
  • Counter current mechanism Is a system in which the inflow runs parallel outflow.


Ganong’s Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No.1573.

questions.stem: The proximal convoluted tubule in the nephron is located between the Bowman's capsule and the loop of the Henle. It serves to resorption of sugar, sodium and chloride ions, and water from the glomerular filtrate. Select the incorrect?

options.label: A
options.text: The tubular fluid remains isosmotic in proximal tubules.

options.label: B
options.text: Solutes and water are reabsorbed in equal proportions, so little change in osmolarity occurs

options.label: C
options.text: Only solutes are reabsorbed from PCT, not water

options.label: D
options.text: Proximal tubule fluid has an osmolarity of about 300 mosm/l

questions.answerText: Only solutes are reabsorbed from PCT, not water
questions.solutionHtml:
Only solutes are reabsorbed from PCT, not water
  • Solutes and water are reabsorbed in equal proportions, so little change in osmolarity occurs in PCT.


Guyton and Hall textbook of physiology, 14th Edition,Page No.366.

questions.stem: Male patients aged 23 years reported to nephrologists with increased thirst, frequent passing large amounts of pale urine, weakness, and lethargy. H/o revealed nocturia for the past 4 months. Select the incorrect?

options.label: A
options.text: ADH increases the water permeability of distal and cortical collecting tubules

options.label: B
options.text: Absence of ADH control on water permeability of distal and cortical collecting tubules

options.label: C
options.text: Passing dilute urine with a large amount of water

options.label: D
options.text: Injury to the hypothalamus or pituitary gland or genetics, or nephrogenic to diabetes insipidus

questions.answerText: Absence of ADH control on water permeability of distal and cortical collecting tubules
questions.solutionHtml:
Absence of ADH control on water permeability of distal and cortical collecting tubules
  • Vasopressin has three main effects which are: increasing the water permeability of distal and cortical collecting tubules (DCT & CCT), as well as outer and inner medullary collecting duct (OMCD & IMCD) in the kidney, thus allowing water reabsorption and excretion of more concentrated urine, i.e., antidiuresis.


Guyton and Hall textbook of physiology, 14th Edition, Page No.366.

questions.stem: Physiologists described to students about the countercurrent mechanism of concentration of urine. He emphasized the role of a high osmolarity of the renal medullary interstitial fluid, which provides the osmotic gradient necessary for water reabsorption. Select the correct for high osmolarity of the renal medullary interstitial fluid?

options.label: A
options.text: Role of countercurrent multiplier

options.label: B
options.text: Role of countercurrent exchanger

options.label: C
options.text: Loop of Henle

options.label: D
options.text: Both a and c correct

questions.answerText: Both a and c correct
questions.solutionHtml:
Both a and c correct
  • Loop of henle is involved in countercurrent multiplier mechanism to create high osmolarity of the renal medullary interstitial fluid.
  • The osmolarity of interstitial fluid in almost all parts of the body is about 300 mosm/l, which is similar to the plasma osmolarity.


Guyton and Hall textbook of physiology, 14th Edition, Page No.368-371.

questions.stem: Physiologists explained the process of water diuresis and osmotic diuresis and their manifestations in patients. Select the incorrect statement not relevant to the difference between two clinical conditions?

options.label: A
options.text: In water diuresis, the volume of water reabsorption in the proximal portions of the nephron is normal,

options.label: B
options.text: Urine output can rise to nearly 16 ml/min in water diuresis

options.label: C
options.text: In osmotic diuresis, water reabsorption in pct is increased but in DCT is reduced

options.label: D
options.text: In osmotic diuresis, urine volume is more than the normal output

questions.answerText: In osmotic diuresis, water reabsorption in pct is increased but in DCT is reduced
questions.solutionHtml:
In osmotic diuresis, water reabsorption in pct is increased but in DCT is reduced
  • In osmotic diuresis, the osmotic concentration of solute is increased in the lumen of pct leading to increased water excretion in urine.


Ganong’s Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No.1577.

questions.stem: Free water clearance by the kidney is increased by which of the following?

options.label: A
options.text: Diabetes insipidus

options.label: B
options.text: Renal failure

options.label: C
options.text: Diuretic therapy

options.label: D
options.text: Diabetes mellitus

questions.answerText: Diabetes insipidus
questions.solutionHtml:
Diabetes insipidus
  • Free water clearance refers to the ability of the kidneys to excrete water without affecting the excretion of electrolytes.
  • Diabetes insipidus is a condition where there is a deficiency of antidiuretic hormone (ADH), which normally helps the kidneys reabsorb water. In the absence of ADH, the kidneys excrete large volumes of dilute urine, leading to an increase in free water clearance.
  • Therefore, the correct answer is A. Diabetes insipidus.


Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition, Page Number: 346.

questions.stem: In renal disease, albumin is first to appear in urine because:

options.label: A
options.text: Of its high concentration in plasma

options.label: B
options.text: Has molecular weight slightly greater than the molecules normally getting filtered

options.label: C
options.text: High albumin: globulin ratio

options.label: D
options.text: Tubular epithelial cells are sensitive to albumin

questions.answerText: Has molecular weight slightly greater than the molecules normally getting filtered
questions.solutionHtml:
Has molecular weight slightly greater than the molecules normally getting filtered
  • The correct answer is B. Has a molecular weight slightly greater than the molecules normally getting filtered.


Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition, Page Number: 361.

questions.stem: Absorption of all occurs in PCT except:

options.label: A
options.text: PO4

options.label: B
options.text: Glucose

options.label: C
options.text: HCO3-

options.label: D
options.text: H+

questions.answerText: PO4
questions.solutionHtml:
PO4
  • Among the options provided, phosphate (PO4) is the only substance that is not absorbed in the PCT. Most of the filtered phosphate is reabsorbed in the more distal parts of the nephron, such as the proximal straight tubule, the loop of Henle, and the distal convoluted tubule.
  • Therefore, the correct answer is A.


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 649

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true?

options.label: A
options.text: Fluid coming from the descending limb of the loop of Henle is hypotonic

options.label: B
options.text: Descending limb of the loop of Henle is permeable to solutes

options.label: C
options.text: If clearance of substance is greater than GFR, then tubular secretion must be present

options.label: D
options.text: Clearance of a substance is always less than GFR if there is a tubular secretion

questions.answerText: If clearance of substance is greater than GFR, then tubular secretion must be present
questions.solutionHtml:
If clearance of substance is greater than GFR, then tubular secretion must be present
  • Option C is true. Clearance of a substance is the rate at which that substance is cleared from the blood by the kidneys and is calculated by dividing the urinary excretion rate of the substance by its plasma concentration.


Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition, Page Number: 346,371 & 401.

questions.stem: Hypertension has been observed in a young boy since birth. Which of the following disorders may be present?

options.label: A
options.text: Bartter’s syndrome

options.label: B
options.text: Gitelman’s syndrome

options.label: C
options.text: Liddle’s syndrome

options.label: D
options.text: Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus

questions.answerText: Liddle’s syndrome
questions.solutionHtml:
Liddle’s syndrome
  • Liddle's syndrome is a rare genetic disorder that causes hypertension from birth or early childhood. It is caused by mutations in the genes that encode for the epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) in the renal tubules. The mutations result in increased activity of ENaC, leading to increased reabsorption of sodium and water by the renal tubules, and ultimately causing hypertension.
  • Therefore, the most likely disorder present in this young boy is C. Liddle's syndrome.


Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 13th Edition, Page Number: 435.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a component of the countercurrent mechanism?

options.label: A
options.text: Thick ascending loop of Henle

options.label: B
options.text: Proximal convoluted tubule

options.label: C
options.text: Vasa recta

options.label: D
options.text: Descending limb of the loop of Henle

questions.answerText: Proximal convoluted tubule
questions.solutionHtml:
Proximal convoluted tubule
  • The countercurrent mechanism is an important process that occurs in the kidneys to establish and maintain the concentration gradient of urine. It involves the interaction between the loops of Henle and the vasa recta.
  • Therefore, the correct answer is B. Proximal convoluted tubule, as this segment of the nephron is not directly involved in the countercurrent mechanism.


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 654
